newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA GOVT SAYS HAS TWO BINDING BIDS FOR SUN AIR.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA GOVT SAYS HAS TWO BINDING BIDS FOR SUN AIR.

text.p: The South African government said on Thursday it had received two binding bids for the 100 percent privatisation of domestic carrier Sun Air and expected to announce the winning bid within weeks.
"The government has received two binding bids from Phoenix and Comair for the privatisation of Sun Air. Discussions with the two companies are still in progress," a government spokesman said.
The announcement was made by Wandile Zote on behalf of the ministers of Transport and Public Enterprises. He said the winning tender was expected to be announced "within the next few weeks."

Comair Consortium and Phoenix Venture Partners Consortium were shortlisted in July along with Malaysia Airlines Consortium and Bhekilanga Consortium as bidders for the airline which operates eight aircraft on routes between Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban.
Transport Minister Mac Maharaj said last month that the non- binding bids had valued the airline between 90-140 million rand.
Virgin Atlantic withdrew from the bidding last month and his since expressed interest in acquiring a stake in South African Airways, which the government aims to part privatise.
